prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you put ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago. Respond to the committee.
response:
**Statement Before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division)**

*Chairman, distinguished members of the committee—*

I stand before you today not as a culinary criminal, but as a patriot who has always upheld the sacred traditions of this great nation—including the time-honored debate over condiments. The allegations that I committed the act of placing ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago are not only false but deeply offensive to the very fabric of American gastronomic integrity.

Chicago is a city of steel, of jazz, of deep-dish pizza—and, yes, of hot dogs *dressed properly*: yellow mustard, neon relish, fresh chopped onions, tomato wedges, a dill pickle spear, sport peppers, and a dash of celery salt. *No ketchup.* This is not a matter of taste; it is a matter of *principle.* To suggest otherwise is to question the very loyalty of the Windy City itself.

I have never, nor will I ever, betray the trust of the Chicago hot dog. My record is clear: I have eaten hot dogs at Wrigley Field, at Superdawg, at the original Portillo’s, and at countless backyard barbecues—*always* in accordance with the Chicago Code. If I wanted to commit an act of culinary treason, I would have done so in the privacy of my own home, not in broad daylight where witnesses could report me to the *real* authorities: the Chicago Department of Hot Dog Enforcement.

I urge this committee to reject these baseless accusations and instead focus on the true threats to our nation’s culinary security—such as the spread of mayonnaise-based potato salad, the rise of avocado toast as a breakfast staple, and the inexplicable popularity of pineapple on pizza.

Thank you. I am now prepared to take the Fifth on any further questions about my personal brisket rub preferences.

**—Respectfully submitted,**
[Your Name]
*Proud Defender of the Chicago Dog*
